title: Transfer of an ample neighbourhood through an affine commutative square
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$, $g:Z\to S$, $a:Y\to Z$, and $b:X\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $g\circ a=b\circ f$. Assume $a$ and $b$ are affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. Let $N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Z$-module and $M$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], with an isomorphism $a^*N\cong M$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Let $V\subseteq S$ be an affine open such that $N|_{g^{-1}(V)}$ is ample in the absolute sense [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Then $U=b^{-1}(V)$ is an affine open of $X$, $f^{-1}(U)$ is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and $M|_{f^{-1}(U)}$ is ample in the absolute sense. Moreover, $M|_{f^{-1}(W)}$ is ample for every affine open $W\subseteq U$.

proof.text: Put $T=g^{-1}(V)$, $U=b^{-1}(V)$, and $Y_0=f^{-1}(U)$. Since $b$ is affine and $V$ is affine open, the definition of an affine morphism gives that $U$ is affine open. Commutativity gives $Y_0=a^{-1}(T)$: for $y\in Y$, $f(y)\in b^{-1}(V)$ if and only if $g(a(y))\in V$. Thus $a$ restricts to $a_0:Y_0\to T$. This restriction is affine directly from the same definition: any affine open $H\subseteq T$ is also an affine open of $Z$, and $a_0^{-1}(H)=a^{-1}(H)$ is affine.

source.place: Tag 0D2S, lemma-ample-in-neighbourhood, final paragraph and hints; affine restriction is Definition 01S6 (morphisms-definition-affine).

proof.text: Write $N_T=N|_T$ and $M_0=M|_{Y_0}$. For the open inclusions $j:T\hookrightarrow Z$ and $i:Y_0\hookrightarrow Y$, restriction agrees with module pullback. The cited pullback lemma gives invertibility of these restrictions and the composition isomorphism. Since $j\circ a_0=a\circ i$, it gives $a_0^*N_T\cong a_0^*j^*N\cong i^*a^*N\cong i^*M\cong M_0$, where the middle isomorphism also uses the given $a^*N\cong M$. By hypothesis $N_T$ is ample, and $a_0$ is affine by step 1. Affine pullback of ampleness therefore makes $a_0^*N_T$ ample. Invariance under module isomorphisms makes $M_0$ ample. The quasi-compactness clause in the definition of absolute ampleness then gives that $Y_0$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0892, lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample (2), affine case used in 0D2S; Sheaves Tags 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules), 00A0 (lemma-j-pullback); Properties Tag 01PS (definition-ample).

proof.text: Let $W\subseteq U$ be any affine open, and let $f_0:Y_0\to U$ be the restriction of $f$. Both $W$ and $U$ are affine, so their inclusion $k:W\hookrightarrow U$ is affine by the affine-schemes morphism lemma. Put $Y_W=f^{-1}(W)$. The square with horizontal maps $r:Y_W\hookrightarrow Y_0$ and $k$, and vertical maps the restrictions of $f$, is Cartesian: a map $H\to Y_0$ factors through the open $Y_W$ precisely when its composite $H\to U$ factors through the open $W$; in either case the factor is unique, with the restricted structure-sheaf map. This verifies the fibre-product universal property. Thus $r$ is the base change of $k$ along $f_0$, and the affine-morphism base-change lemma shows that $r$ is affine.

source.place: Tags 01SH (lemma-morphism-affines-affine) and 01SD (lemma-base-change-affine), applied to W into U; open subschemes and the fibre-product universal property give the displayed square.

proof.text: Apply affine pullback of ampleness to $r$ and the ample invertible module $M_0$ from step 2. It gives that $r^*M_0$ is ample. If $i_W:Y_W\hookrightarrow Y$ is the inclusion, then $i\circ r=i_W$. Open restriction and the pullback-composition isomorphism give $r^*M_0\cong r^*i^*M\cong i_W^*M\cong M|_{Y_W}$; these are invertible by the pullback lemma. Invariance under isomorphisms proves that $M|_{f^{-1}(W)}$ is ample, as required for every such $W$.

source.place: Tag 0892, lemma-pullback-ample-tensor-relatively-ample (2), second affine pullback; Sheaves Tags 0097 and 00A0; Properties Definition 01PS.
